Revision 0: April 28, 2017 Country of Publication: India Page 1a) Homage to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
Sandalwood, agallochum, camphor, tamāla, water, and saffron.
Kuśīta, combined with kuṣṭha, is known as the eightfold fragrance of Śiva (śaivagandhāṣṭaka). || 1 ||
Sandalwood, agallochum, camphor, *tālīśa* water, saffron, costus, and red sandalwood. || 2 ||
Sandalwood, agallochum, hni-vera, kuṣṭha, saffron, and sevyaka.
Jaṭāmāṃsī and Surabhi are known as the eight fragrances of Viṣṇu.
Sandalwood, agallochum, vālaka, kuṅkuma, śvetavirā, mūla, jaṭāmāṃsī, and devadāru— these are known as the eight fragrances (gandhāṣṭaka) of Viṣṇu.
Svarūpa, candana, cora, rocanā, and aguru as well. || 4 ||
Who is the deer-marked one, the moon, joined with the constellation Mṛgaśiras?
The eightfold incense of the great lord Gaṇeśa has been fully described.
Sandalwood, agallochum, camphor, coraka, saffron, and gorocana.
Jaṭāmāṃsī together with Kapi—these they know as the eight fragrances for the sake of power.
The thief, the crow, the rogue, the thief’s son, and the one who serves the enemy—these are the enemies.
Silūka, kapija, dhūmra, turuṣka, piṇḍikavi, and silājīta. || 7 || Silājīta.
One should place the lamp to the right, or in front, or behind.
Likewise, the incense-burner should be on the left, while the water-vessel is in front or to the right.
The food offering (naivedya) is placed to the right, to the left, in front, on the ground, or behind the deity.
He placed the *nivara* grain in his right ear and likewise in his left, and thus he offered it at the beginning.
This rite is for the twice-born; for women and Śūdras, it is in the Vāmaka [tradition].
p. 2) The giving of mantras.
Through your grace, O God, I have accomplished all that was to be done in every respect.
"I am liberated from the great snare of illusory death; I am Śiva. || 1 ||

Thus the disciple should say: "Arise! You are truly consecrated; be one who possesses correct conduct. Through *hrī*, may splendor, beauty, sons, longevity, strength, and health always abide in you. (2)
Thus the Guru should say. This concludes the procedure for the bestowal of mantras according to the Mahākālasaṃhitā.

May there be well-being! This book was copied on the 14th day of the dark fortnight of the month of Jyeṣṭha, in the year 1952 of the Śrī Saṃvat, on the 5th solar day (roja), by the twice-born Dharmarāja Tripāṭhī, for his own benefit and for the benefit of others.
